message.content:
**Typical difference:**  
- **Los Angeles (Pacific Time)** is UTC‑8 in winter and UTC‑7 in summer.  
- **Berlin (Central European Time)** is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer.  

Because both regions shift their clocks by the same amount (one hour forward in spring, one hour back in autumn), the time difference is normally **9 hours** (Berlin is ahead).

**When the difference changes:**  
The U.S. and the EU change their clocks on slightly different dates:

| Period | U.S. DST | EU DST | Difference |
|--------|----------|--------|------------|
| **Before U.S. DST starts** (early March) | Standard (UTC‑8) | Standard (UTC+1) | 9 h |
| **After U.S. DST starts, before EU DST starts** (mid‑March to end‑March) | DST (UTC‑7) | Standard (UTC+1) | **8 h** |
| **After EU DST starts, before U.S. DST ends** (late October to early November) | DST (UTC‑7) | Standard (UTC+1) | **8 h** |
| **All other times** | DST (UTC‑7) | DST (UTC+2) | 9 h |

So, for most of the year Berlin is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles, but during the brief windows when only one side is observing daylight‑saving time the gap shrinks to 8 hours.

In winter, Los Angeles UTC-8, Berlin UTC+1, difference 9 hours. So constant 9 hours. But if we consider times of year when one is DST and other not? They both observe DST but start/stop at different dates. There might be a period where difference is 8 or 10 hours. So there is overlap: from March 8 to March 31? Actually US DST starts earlier (second Sunday March). EU DST starts later (last Sunday March). So between US DST start and EU DST start, Los Angeles is on DST (UTC-7) while Berlin still on standard (UTC+1). So difference is 8 hours. Similarly, after EU DST ends (last Sunday Oct) but before US DST ends (first Sunday Nov), Berlin is on standard (UTC+1) while Los Angeles still on DST (UTC-7). So difference is 8 hours. Wait: After EU DST ends, Berlin goes back to UTC+1, Los Angeles still on DST until first Sunday Nov. So difference: Berlin UTC+1, Los Angeles UTC-7 => 8 hours.
